name: NPZ Class Map export resolves overlaps to lowest class and stores foreground
given: An image img.png of height 2 and width 3 (H=2, W=3). Labelled pixels: class id 7 covers (row 0, col 0) and (row 0, col 1); class id 2 covers (row 0, col 1) only; every other pixel is unlabelled. NPZ Class Map is among the selected export formats. Pixel Priority is off (settings pixel_priority_enabled = false). class_order is NOT free-form: every live caller passes the per-image list of unique class ids sorted ascending by SegmentManager.get_unique_class_ids (legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/segment_manager.py:87-95), from save_export_manager.py:400 and :494 and main_window.py:6602 — so class_order = [2, 7], meaning channel 0 = class 2 and channel 1 = class 7. The mask tensor is (H, W, C) uint8 holding only 0 or 1: it is allocated as np.zeros(dtype=np.uint8) and filled with np.logical_or per channel (segment_manager.py:223, 242-244), so here channel 0 = [[0,1,0],[0,0,0]] and channel 1 = [[1,1,0],[0,0,0]]. class_aliases is the whole session alias dict, not just this image's classes (save_export_manager.py:424; main_window.py:6622): {2: 'cat', 7: 'dog'}.
when: export_all runs the NPZ Class Map exporter over that context (legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/exporters/npz_class_map.py:20-44). It returns None and writes nothing when mask_tensor.size == 0 or when no element is > 0 (lines 21-26). Otherwise it builds class_map by taking np.argmax over the channel axis and indexing a uint16 lookup table built from class_order (lines 66-73), builds foreground = np.any(mask_tensor > 0, axis=2) (line 33), creates the parent directory (line 36) and writes one np.savez_compressed archive (lines 37-43).
then: One file is written at the image path with its extension stripped plus '_CM.npz' — img_CM.npz (npz_class_map.py:46-47) — containing exactly four arrays (lines 37-43). class_map = [[7, 2, 0], [0, 0, 0]], dtype uint16: pixel A (0,0) = 7 because only channel 1 is active and class_order[1] = 7; pixel B (0,1) = 2 because both channels hold 1 and np.argmax returns the FIRST maximum, channel 0, and class_order[0] = 2; pixel C (0,2) and all of row 1 = 0 because no channel is active there, so they keep the np.zeros fill (lines 67-72). foreground = [[true, true, false], [false, false, false]], dtype bool (line 33). class_order = [2, 7], dtype int64 (line 41: np.array over the Python int list; int64 on this platform under NumPy 2.x). class_aliases = {2: 'cat', 7: 'dog'} (line 42). I reproduced lines 66-73 verbatim in memory under NumPy 2.2.6 and got exactly class_map [7, 2, 0] and foreground [true, true, false].
and: Reloading img.png when no img.npz, img_seg.txt and img_coco.json sit beside it (FileManager._LOAD_CHAIN, file_manager.py:128-136) reads img_CM.npz through load_npz_class_map (file_manager.py:282-333) with image_size = (2, 3), in this order: the archive is opened (line 297), the class_map key is required (lines 298-300), foreground is data['foreground'].astype(bool) or, if the key is absent, class_map != 0 (lines 303-307), class_aliases is restored — REPLACING the whole session dict with {int(k): v} (line 308, _restore_aliases at lines 335-343) — and only then is the shape gate applied (lines 313-318). Here tuple(class_map.shape[:2]) == (2, 3) so the gate passes, and one segment is added per value of np.unique(class_map[foreground]) in ascending class-id order (lines 320-331): first class_id 2 with mask [[false, true, false], [false, false, false]] (1 pixel), then class_id 7 with mask [[true, false, false], [false, false, false]] (1 pixel), each {type: 'Loaded', vertices: null, class_id: int(value)}. The round trip is lossy by design: class 7 loses the overlap pixel B, a class whose pixels are all covered by lower ids disappears entirely, and per-object separation is gone — exactly one segment per distinct class id.
parameters: Output path: os.path.splitext(image_path)[0] + '_CM.npz'; parent directory created if missing (npz_class_map.py:36, 46-47). Four keys are always written, never a subset (lines 37-43): class_map (H, W) uint16 with 0 as background; foreground (H, W) bool; class_order (C,) int64; class_aliases dict[int, str] — legacy writes it as a pickled object array, the rewrite writes it as a JSON string (see answer). Valid class id range is 0..65535 inclusive: np.array(class_order, dtype=np.uint16) at line 71 raises OverflowError ('Python integer 65536 out of bounds for uint16') for any id > 65535 or < 0 under numpy>=2.1.2 (legacy/lazylabel/pyproject.toml:23) — verified on NumPy 2.2.6. It does NOT wrap around, and export_all does not catch it (exporters/__init__.py:189-206), so the class map and every format iterated after it in the non-deterministic set order are skipped. Overlap tie-break: np.argmax over axis 2 = the FIRST channel holding the maximum value; because the tensor is strictly 0/1 this is the first ACTIVE channel, and it equals 'lowest class id' only because class_order is sorted ascending — with an unsorted order [7, 2] the same pixel B becomes 7 (verified in memory). Pixel Priority is applied to the tensor before the exporter sees it (segment_manager.py:247-250, 317-373), never inside the exporter: ascending (the default) leaves B = 2 via argmin; descending makes B = 7 via argmax (lines 356-361). Loader constants: the shape gate compares only class_map.shape[:2] against (height, width) (file_manager.py:313-318) and is skipped when image_size is None, which production never does because load_existing_mask resolves the size first (file_manager.py:178-185); the foreground key name is exactly 'foreground' and its absence falls back to class_map != 0 (lines 303-307), it is never combined with that test.
edgeCases: Empty or all-zero mask tensor: the exporter returns None and writes NO NEW file (npz_class_map.py:21-26). It does not delete. export_all never deletes (exporters/__init__.py:189-206), so a stale img_CM.npz written by an earlier save survives on disk and will be reloaded later. Files are removed only when the image has zero segments at all (save_export_manager.py:106-109 and main_window.py:6589-6594, via delete_all_outputs at exporters/__init__.py:209-215). The card's 'No file when no pixel is labelled' must be read as 'no new file written', not 'no file exists'.

Crop interaction: an active crop zeroes every pixel outside the crop box while keeping the (H, W, C) shape (file_manager._apply_crop_to_mask, file_manager.py:712-739) and is applied BEFORE the exporter's emptiness check (save_export_manager.py:412-417). A crop that excludes every labelled pixel therefore produces the stale-file case above with no warning.

Class id above 65535 or below 0: np.array(class_order, dtype=np.uint16) raises OverflowError at npz_class_map.py:71 and the save fails; it does not wrap. Reachable in practice because ids are taken from annotation files with no range check — file_manager.py:643 int(ann.get('category_id', 0)) for COCO and file_manager.py:366 int(label) for numeric labels.

Class id 0 is indistinguishable from background in class_map alone; only the foreground key recovers it (npz_class_map.py:30-33; file_manager.py:303-307). The default id for a new class is 0 (segment_manager.py:16, 24), so this is the common case, not a corner. A third-party or pre-2.0.8 file with no foreground key silently drops every class-0 annotation on reload (guarded by tests/unit/core/exporters/test_bbox_roundtrip.py:566-578).
Third-party readers that ignore the foreground key cannot tell class 0 from background; the key is deliberately additive (npz_class_map.py:30-32).

Shape mismatch: a class_map of shape (3, 2) loaded against a 2x3 image (or a 240x320 map against a 480x640 image) logs an error and adds ZERO segments, returning normally rather than raising (file_manager.py:313-318). Test: test_bbox_roundtrip.py:580-589.

Rejection has a side effect the card omitted: _restore_aliases runs at file_manager.py:308, BEFORE the shape gate at :313, so a rejected class map still replaces the whole session class_aliases dict (file_manager.py:343 assigns, it does not merge).

Rejection stops the fallback chain — known legacy defect, do NOT reproduce. Because load_npz_class_map returns normally instead of raising, load_existing_mask reaches its return at file_manager.py:205 and never tries the lower-priority .xml, _createml.json or .txt sidecars. The same happens for a missing class_map key (:298-300) and for OSError/ValueError (:309-311). This contradicts the method's own docstring (file_manager.py:161-163) and CHANGELOG.md:24. Auto-save on navigate is on by default (config/settings.py:45 auto_save = True; file_navigation_manager.py:156-160), and an empty segment list makes the next save delete every annotation file for that image (save_export_manager.py:106-109) — the exact data loss CHANGELOG.md:12 claims was fixed.

Asymmetric failure: a foreground array whose shape does not match class_map raises IndexError at file_manager.py:320, OUTSIDE the try/except at :296-311. load_existing_mask's broad except at :202-204 catches it and DOES continue to the next format — but only after the aliases at :308 were already replaced.

_CM.npz is only ever read when no img.npz, img_seg.txt and img_coco.json exist (file_manager.py:128-136, mirroring exporters.LOAD_PRIORITY at exporters/__init__.py:73-81). Since the default export set is {NPZ, YOLO_DETECTION} (exporters/__init__.py:60-63) and exporting never deletes, an img.npz normally wins and the class map is never read back.
Reload loses overlap data: the class that lost the argmax tie-break loses those pixels permanently, and a class entirely covered by lower ids vanishes from the reloaded segment list.
Per-object separation is lost: exactly one segment per distinct class id, mask = foreground AND class_map == id (file_manager.py:320-331). Two separate objects of one class come back fused.

Reloaded segments are added in ascending class-id order (np.unique), with class_id = int(value), type 'Loaded' and vertices null (file_manager.py:320-331). The guard 'if not np.any(class_mask): continue' at :322-323 is unreachable, since every id came from class_map[foreground].

class_aliases is the full session dict, not filtered to class_order, and may legitimately be {} — get_class_alias falls back to str(class_id) for unnamed classes (segment_manager.py:397-399; save_export_manager.py:424).

The exporter accepts an unsorted or non-contiguous class_order and would then make the FIRST-listed class win overlaps (verified: order [7, 2] gives pixel B = 7). No live code constructs such an order; SaveWorker would allow one but is never instantiated anywhere in src (only re-exported at ui/workers/__init__.py:15, 28). The rewrite must keep the ascending sort or state the rule as 'first channel wins'.

Security: legacy opens the archive with allow_pickle=True (file_manager.py:297) purely to read the pickled class_aliases dict, so a crafted _CM.npz can execute code on open. Per the approved decision, no rewrite code path may unpickle.
answer: Open question, answered: the card's export Given/When/Then is in fact faithful — I re-ran npz_class_map.py:66-73 verbatim under NumPy 2.2.6 with class_order [2, 7] and got class_map [7, 2, 0] and foreground [true, true, false] exactly as written; the fidelity judge's 'faithful no' verdict applies to a different folded sub-card (the import/size-mismatch scenario, P0_PANEL.md 'NPZ Class Map import requires matching size'), whose Given described a foreground key covering only some 0-valued pixels, which would make np.unique(class_map[foreground]) return [0] and produce no class-4 segment at all (file_manager.py:320) — that scenario is replaced here by the concrete 2x3 round trip in 'and'. On the product-choice half: class_aliases must be written as a JSON string with string keys and read back as {int(k): v} to match legacy's _restore_aliases normalisation (file_manager.py:343); class_map (uint16), foreground (bool) and class_order (int64) stay array-identical to legacy (npz_class_map.py:37-43); per-image class ids and aliases stay as legacy computes them (segment_manager.py:87-95; save_export_manager.py:400, :424); and no reader may enable pickle — a legacy file read with pickling disabled still yields class_map, foreground and class_order correctly and raises ValueError only on the class_aliases key (verified), so the reader must catch that one key and treat aliases as absent, falling back to str(class_id) (segment_manager.py:397-399). What was wrong in the card: (1) edge case 'Class IDs above 65535 overflow' is false — np.array(class_order, dtype=np.uint16) at npz_class_map.py:71 raises OverflowError under numpy>=2.1.2 (pyproject.toml:23) and nothing catches it in export_all (exporters/__init__.py:189-206); it never wraps, and negative ids fail the same way; this also duplicated edge case 4, so the two are merged; (2) 'No file when no pixel is labelled' is misleading — nothing new is written but nothing is deleted either (npz_class_map.py:21-26 with exporters/__init__.py:189-206), so a stale img_CM.npz survives, including when a crop blanks every pixel before the check (file_manager.py:712-739 applied at save_export_manager.py:412-417); (3) 'tie-break = lowest class' is only true downstream of the ascending sort at segment_manager.py:87-95 — the exporter itself picks the first CHANNEL (argmax, line 70), which coincides with the lowest id only because callers sort, and is the first ACTIVE channel only because the tensor is strictly 0/1 (segment_manager.py:223, 242-244); (4) the card's Given fixed 'Pixel Priority off' without saying that descending priority flips the winner to 7 before the exporter runs (segment_manager.py:356-361); (5) 'and' was null and the card's import edge cases had no scenario, so the whole reload half (file_manager.py:282-333) is now specified; (6) the rejection path was understated — aliases are replaced at file_manager.py:308 before the shape gate at :313, and a rejected file returns normally so load_existing_mask stops at :205 instead of trying .xml/_createml.json/.txt, contradicting its own docstring at :161-163. Implementers must watch three things: keep the ascending class_order sort or the overlap winner silently changes; always write the foreground key, because class id 0 is the default (segment_manager.py:16, 24) and dropping it deletes every class-0 label on reload (file_manager.py:303-307); and do not port the chain-stop at file_manager.py:205 — combined with auto_save = True (config/settings.py:45; file_navigation_manager.py:156-160) it lets one rejected sidecar empty the segment list and trigger delete_all_outputs on the next save (save_export_manager.py:106-109).
corrections: Recorded that the export Given/When/Then is faithful as written (re-verified against npz_class_map.py:66-73 under NumPy 2.2.6); the 'faithful no' verdict belongs to the folded import sub-card, not to this scenario
Made Given concrete and complete: 2x3 image, explicit per-channel 0/1 uint8 tensor, and the precondition that class_order is get_unique_class_ids() sorted ascending (segment_manager.py:87-95)
Made When name the two early-return guards (mask_tensor.size == 0, no element > 0) at npz_class_map.py:21-26
Kept Then as a worked example but added the two keys the card omitted — class_order (int64) and class_aliases — plus explicit dtypes for all four arrays (npz_class_map.py:37-43)

Filled the previously null 'and' with the reload half: load order gate, alias restore before the shape gate, ascending np.unique segment emission, and the lossy overlap round trip (file_manager.py:128-136, 282-333)
Replaced 'dtype uint16 (class IDs up to 65535)' with the exact range 0..65535 inclusive and the hard OverflowError failure mode, including that export_all does not catch it
Restated the tie-break as 'first channel via argmax', valid as 'lowest class id' only under the ascending sort; added the unsorted-order counterexample (order [7,2] gives B = 7)
Added Pixel Priority as a parameter: applied to the tensor before export, ascending keeps 2, descending gives 7 (segment_manager.py:247-250, 356-361)
Deleted the false edge case 'Class IDs above 65535 overflow' and merged it with the correct one; added that negative ids fail identically
Qualified 'No file when no pixel is labelled' as 'no new file written, stale file retained', and added the crop path that reaches it
Added the rejection side effect: class_aliases is replaced at file_manager.py:308 before the shape check at :313
Added the chain-stop defect (file_manager.py:205 vs its docstring at :161-163 and CHANGELOG.md:24) and its data-loss consequence via auto-save + delete_all_outputs, flagged as not-to-be-ported
Added the asymmetric IndexError path for a mis-shaped foreground array (file_manager.py:320, outside the try), which does continue the chain
Added the precondition that _CM.npz is only read when no .npz/_seg.txt/_coco.json exists (file_manager.py:128-136)
Added reload ordering, int() coercion, type 'Loaded'/vertices null, and the unreachable empty-mask guard at file_manager.py:322-323
Added that class_aliases is the whole session dict (possibly empty) and that restoring replaces rather than merges

Answered the alias-storage decision: JSON string with string keys, read back as int keys; legacy arrays unchanged; reading a legacy file with pickling disabled succeeds for all three arrays and fails only on the class_aliases key, which must then be treated as absent
unresolved: Three behaviour choices sit outside the approved NPZ-format decision and need the product owner. (1) When a _CM.npz is rejected (shape mismatch, missing class_map key, unreadable archive), should the loader continue to the lower-priority .xml / _createml.json / .txt sidecars instead of stopping as legacy does at file_manager.py:205? The legacy stop, combined with default auto-save, can delete healthy ground truth. (2) Should a rejected file still be allowed to overwrite the session's class aliases (file_manager.py:308 running before the gate at :313)? (3) Should a save whose mask tensor is empty after cropping delete the stale _CM.npz rather than leaving an out-of-date file that will be reloaded (npz_class_map.py:21-26 with exporters/__init__.py:189-206)? Separately, writing class_aliases as a JSON string is a one-way compatibility break: legacy LazyLabel reading a new file hits AttributeError in _restore_aliases (file_manager.py:343, since .item() returns a str) and, caught by load_existing_mask at :202-204, skips the class map entirely and falls through to the next format — confirm that losing legacy-reader compatibility for new files is acceptable.
